instruction_and_reasoning: Cost behavior and traceability are separated from relevant future differences; fixed amounts may be avoidable while sunk cost is not a future saving. Future resale proceeds and alternative use are included once.

Break-even formulas state contribution, mix, relevant range, integer and capacity conditions. The step-cost exercise correctly compares feasible branch maxima rather than applying a global linear formula.
All fixed pools reconcile under both actual-hour allocation and practical-capacity ABC. Unused capacity remains a company cost, not a payment automatically avoided by dropping a product.

For 300 hours, 30x+60y=12(2x+5y)+6x<=4080, with equality uniquely at (80,28). At 400 hours, rounded batch feasibility implies y<=60-x/5 and contribution<=3600+18x<=5040, attained only at (80,44). Demand and setup feasibility are explicitly checked.

At 301 hours the objective is a multiple of 30 and its continuous bound is 4092; therefore contribution cannot exceed 4080. Equality candidates (80,28) and (78,29) are feasible. Integer increments need not match the relaxation slope.

Idle and busy special orders use explicitly different regular demand facts. Busy opportunity cost compares optimally reconfigured feasible regular plans; the separate setup and external payment are neither omitted nor double-counted.

Make/buy and inventory cases are explicitly separate from the main operating ledger. Absorption and variable presentations share cash and physical facts; only fixed manufacturing expense timing differs.
Risk-neutral expected private benefit, expected external harm, certification and funding feasibility remain distinct. The open explanation questions state what evidence earns credit.

Methods required by every exercise are taught before use; all requested calculations and explanations are addressed. Teaching and retention prompts have actual benchmarks. Canonical prerequisite acceptance and whole-site integration remain coordinator tasks.

limitations: Peer review checks the stated synthetic economics, arithmetic, instructional logic and inspected source scopes. It is not external human certification or a full current accounting-standards audit.

The lab is a finite two-product internal before-tax model. Demand, quality, driver appropriateness, avoidability and alternative-use contribution are supplied facts, not estimated or verified business evidence.

The lab validates enough opening cash for all regular demand but does not model dated funding for arbitrary edited special-order commitments, uncertainty or financing. Decisions with changed timing or cash constraints require those consequences to be added, as the chapter states.
No browser, mobile, visual or print QA performed. Whole-library structural integration, source registration and prerequisite-ordered acceptance remain coordinator tasks.
